title: Basic Merge Conflict
objective: Resolve a two-branch, one-file merge conflict so that both branches' changes to the same line are preserved in the final result.
description: The lab starts with two branches that edited the same line differently. Merge feature/login into main, read the conflict markers, combine the requirements, and complete the merge commit.

lesson.principle: A merge combines intent, not just lines. A stricter password minimum also satisfies the earlier minimum.
lesson.question: Main requires a password of at least 8 characters. The feature requires a user name of at least 3 and a password of at least 12. Which final rule keeps both requirements?
options: User name at least 3 and password at least 12
lesson.explanation: The 12-character minimum includes main's 8-character minimum, while the user name rule preserves the feature change.
pitfalls: Leaving conflict marker lines in login.go.
Keeping only main's return line and losing the user name check.
Editing the file without staging and committing the merge.

hints: Run the merge and study the output carefully; Git tells you exactly which file is in conflict before you open anything.
Open the conflicted file and locate the <<<<<<<, =======, and >>>>>>> markers; each side of the marker block is one branch's version of the line.
Edit the file to keep both changes in a sensible order, remove all three marker lines, then git add the file and commit to finish the merge.
